preconditions: Owned native Linux project with checked journal, released original writer lock and a transaction-bound recovery lock; synthetic explicit host authorization.
Explicit transaction-bound host authority; real stopped Linux processes and native root mutex for orphan recovery; independent normative byte oracle.
Recovery derivative publication requires native Linux O_TMPFILE support and a usable /proc/self/fd link; unsupported operations fail without a named-write fallback.

Restore-plan subset: original full-project source and independently inventoried current bytes, with synthetic sealed Baselines and native bound Evidence; no restore execution or durable audit is asserted.
steps: Complete a full target or roll back a partial publication; verify immutable authority-attributed action evidence.
Discard an unpublished preparation and check its receipt link to retained audit bytes.
Explicitly archive terminal work; verify action, journal, intent and complete retained file-inventory bindings.
Retry under a second authorized caller without replacing the first audit attribution; refuse conflicting existing evidence.
Interrupt terminal evidence and archive durability; retain original audit attribution, short/conflicting evidence and active pending barriers.
Abruptly stop a native writer and recovery process; verify immutable takeover intent/completion binding old/new owners, journal, authority and risk decision.
Reject altered bindings, authority, live owners and an occupied native mutex; preserve a concurrently changed owner at the transfer boundary.

Interrupt the remaining nine bound recovery derivative writes, repeat native interruptions and abruptly stop processes; resume with audited native lock takeover, retain original images and prove independent basis/full-target bytes without a second normative replacement.

Reject foreign empty/short/conflicting or unsafe files and concurrent prefix collisions; recheck journal, lock, live normative bytes and prior evidence before publication. Reuse complete records without changing their authority attribution; finish existing preserving cleanup.

In fresh writer/recovery processes, reconstruct explicit building/prepared discard inputs and retain the original immutable audit and receipt through selected interrupted completion boundaries; compare independent basis bytes, repeated results and next-writer access.

Bind younger supported protected records and their original dependencies in the passive restore preservation/target inventory; reconstruct it independently and retain negative/stale findings without an execution claim.

Close retained Baseline history before selecting exact Evidence dependency bytes; reject incompatible immutable identities and attachment bindings with code 6, unavailable originals with code 3, and rehashed plans that hide protected records in backup only.

Execute both qualified full source kinds with explicit selected corrupt trees, empty files/directories or no old journal; independently prove the actual full target root, complete original backup objects/directories and audit-before-archive ordering.

Bind current authority, independent target, plan/source/complete inventory, normalized selection and exact own file layout before the first operational write, and repeat under the actual shared kernel mutex. Denied, stale, reused ordinary requests and unselected or malformed/forbidden journal selections remain write-free.

Retain native completed receipts at their original paths; verify exact supported historical result bytes rather than dropping their publication proof. Remove a mutable unprotected addition only with complete backup.

Inject real before/after-replacement I/O failure and a foreign file inside the own backup namespace: preserve original bytes, actual publication and active barrier, refuse blind repeats; do not report recovery completion.

Abruptly exit real isolated processes after bound initial intent, backup, staging, prepared/committing markers, partial/full target writes including replacement-before-sync, completion audit, original-journal and final journal archival. Reopen under fresh authority and original request; match complete actual inventory, never a claimed cursor.

Roll back only a proven partial target from original byte objects, preserving selected original journals and recovery barriers; reverse both new-file/new-directory creation and original-file removal. Finish an exact full target with unavailable external source without republishing normative files. Replay only matching immutable completion; a changed target remains a conflict.

Explicitly transfer a valid selected old transaction owner or matching interrupted Restore owner using the real mutex, expected raw owner hash, independent current takeover authorization, preserved old/new requests and immutable handoff files. Stop live owners and held mutexes even with force; foreign, unverifiable and reused-PID owners require explicit current risk consent.

Repeat crashes during owner replacement, handoff completion and rollback publication, including before sync and before the first main Restore intent. Retain actual state and require fresh authorization each time. Missing/corrupt backup, mismatched selection/target/intent, foreign own-namespace bytes, denied or mutated authority and incomplete arguments remain write-free preflight failures.

Change the external source inside the native committing-marker publication boundary with zero or nonzero target effects: do not publish committing or target bytes. These are selected native boundaries, not complete CLI/Work or all-I/O acceptance.

A matching selected ordinary transaction owner cannot replace the owner of an already begun Restore. Only the exact original owner proved by an incomplete pre-journal handoff is eligible; other ordinary owners conflict without writes.

Publish the fully qualified original plan to one explicit external create-only target through native generated-output and durable image primitives; bind source, inventory, project/root/parent identities and complete staged bytes immediately before publication and verify the final bytes. Existing output and unsafe paths never authorize replacement or project writes.

Read exact external plan and original journal-selection bytes through native descriptors, reconstruct their closed passive contracts and reread both files. Do not confuse this with current source/inventory preflight: the unchanged original plan remains readable after execution or external source loss for the separate specialized recovery path.

Execute both source kinds from the returned exact file inputs using separately supplied current synthetic host authority; confirm old selected journal archival, unchanged input bytes and full target outcome. Native execution remains the only writer and still enforces its current gates.

Inject stale/racing source, inventory, roots, parent, staged image and target, external mutex conflict, I/O failure and isolated process exits before/after atomic file publication. Require byte-exact project preservation and either retained private staging or complete output, without claiming CLI/Work or exhaustive crash coverage.

Exchange opened source/target parents before native Restore publication, removal, selected-journal archival, terminal-journal archival and empty-directory rollback cleanup. Use byte-identical replacement trees, disappearance, symlinks and retained original file inodes with foreign entries in the detached tree. Verify rejection before additional byte, mode or namespace effects in either tree.

Exchange the source or target parent after the staged final mode has been synchronized and before replacement; the repeated binding check must still prevent publication. Unchanged-parent controls retain exact original archival bytes and ordinary final-mode semantics.

Run both qualified source kinds through the actual Restore executor, replace an opened target parent after durable backup and committing evidence, and require code 6 with mutation_possible/recovery_required. Preserve all non-owner bytes, staging, backup and active barrier; the live process may release only its exact temporary owner as already specified.

Bind explicit mutually exclusive Restore planning and execution modes through argv and the native structured CommandRequest grammar. Reject missing, repeated, mixed, malformed or untrusted options, incomplete selection/owner tuples and unsafe lexical roots before any file access; require AI/CI request IDs without deriving permission from actor labels.

Publish native byte-identical complete plans from both explicitly chosen source kinds, including independently retained evidence for missing or damaged configuration. Preserve project and source bytes, use explicit baseline operational values and roots in a new process/working directory, and reject source-kind fallback, output overwrite and unsafe root links.

Read original plan/selection files passively, bind the actual selected project root and independent target, and invoke the existing native execution gates under fresh separate synthetic host authority. Independently verify restored target root, exact selection, backup/audit identity and replay without duplicate durable publication and with renewed authorization; reject missing/denied/invalid authority and stale initial source/inventory.

After real abrupt partial or full target publication, remove the source and resume through both invocation representations with explicit original files and exact owner takeover. Require the native full-target completion or before-image rollback with retained recovery barrier and separate current authorization identity; reject root inode substitution between input reading and native execution.

Inject native EIO/ENOSPC, zero-write, response-loss and fsync failures before and after immutable backup/staging publication, target replacement, journal archival and explicit rollback. Verify actual remaining bytes, original journal/backup preservation, error 5 with mutation/recovery flags, freshly authorized full-target completion or exact original rollback, and no duplicated durable effects.

Bind an independent active terminal barrier to the original unchanged execution journal and request. Preserve the ordinary recovery gate across the terminal directory rename and both-parent durability confirmation; remove only that exact barrier after the complete terminal state is verified. Reject foreign, linked and differently bound barrier bytes without writes.

Resume original legacy active or terminal executions without rewriting their original journal, plan or audit identity. Full-target completion remains independent of source availability; resynchronization faults and repeated rollback failures retain verifiable state. This is targeted R durability coverage, not complete public CLI/Work or release acceptance.

Bind passive recover.restore execution requests to their original native plan bytes and canonical explicit journal selection in the Work input manifest. Reopen a real durable checkpoint chain without reading vanished external transport/source files or invoking a handler; reject altered original actor/request/project/target, missing byte objects, unknown formats and consistent foreign successor rebinding. This is an inert codec/storage subset, not current Restore authorization or Work execution.

Execute the closed Restore Work order from its original stored plan/selection while retaining the external Work inode mutex. Verify actual native target, original backups and separate current Recovery actors. Reject foreign original actors, stale inputs, unbound tasks/progress/build, stale stored takeover and denied or mutating host authority. Abrupt subprocess exits must retain Work bytes and native journals, finish only a proven full target or roll back only a partial target after source loss, without second publication or Work completion.

Recover only an explicitly selected orphan outer Restore Work owner under the retained native inode mutex and independently validated checkpoint chain. Preserve exact old and new bytes in immutable intent/completion records; use current host/boot/PID-namespace and process-start evidence, never stored consent. Exercise real process exits before and after atomic exchange and completion, stale hashes, live/foreign/unknown identities, unsafe files, corrupt or missing records and post-exchange errors. Work progress and native project Restore authority remain separate.

Advance the closed Restore Work execution unit under one continuously held outer owner and inode mutex, with fresh independent native project recovery authorization. Bind the proven native completion in generation one while result delivery remains pending. Check real process exits before and after project and Work publication, lost sources, rollback without progress, missing or contradictory native proof, retained handoff history and late Work changes. Preserve actual project and checkpoint effects on failure.

Complete native Restore execution and output under the same Work owner and inode mutex. Persist the whole native payload and hashed external manifest before confirming the delivery unit and terminal checkpoint. Check actual subprocess exits at both output files and both final pointers, current denial before completion, rollback without delivery, lost output, altered final payloads and late Work changes. Completed replay returns original stored output without invoking native project execution or fresh project/source inspection.

oracle.requirement_contract: Jede ausgeführte Recovery-Aktion MUSS einen unveränderbaren lokalen Auditdatensatz einschließlich der für Restore nach Kapitel 10.7.1 gebundenen Quellen-, Erhaltungs- und Zielinventur erzeugen.
oracle.scope: Immutable evidence for explicit complete-target recovery, rollback, unpublished discard, work cleanup and transaction-bound orphan takeover under native locks. Original authority, owner/journal bindings and retained work inventories survive full-byte durability loss and real process stops. Hash consistency is not authentication. Bound rollback copies, cursor/terminal journals, completion receipts/marker and action/rollback receipts are published only after complete staging. Initial allocation/write failures expose no short canonical helper. Tested repeated native failures and real process stops remain explicitly resumable; foreign or altered bindings block publication, existing evidence retains its bytes and original authority, and mutation diagnostics retain possible operational changes. Selected persisted-input discard restart cases retain the original audit/receipt and complete basis without normative writes; interrupted completion resumes in a fresh process and preserves conflicting evidence. The passive restore subset additionally binds source/preservation/target byte inventories for supported immutable history. Comprehensive Restore fault-injection and complete interrupted-action acceptance remain outside this scope. R-46 Evidence/Baseline cases additionally verify order-independent exact archived attachment selection, shared dependency deduplication and precise conflict/missing-byte diagnostics without modifying historical records or current mutable subjects. Initial Restore now emits an immutable native action audit linking the original plan/source/inventory, preservation and backup hashes, normalized selected original journals, actor/request and current host authority. Before/after-publication failure retains originals and the active blocker; archive moves occur only after full target and durable audit. This is no successful restart or release evidence. Native R recovery now derives only complete inventory-explained effect prefixes, independently authorizes rollback/completion and bound owner takeover, preserves original actors/requests and immutable before images, and checks exact current target on replay. Recovery actors and stale-source observation are separate audit data. No partial-target forward resume or blanket audit-directory exemption is permitted. External Restore plan publication and passive file-input reconstruction now have native behavior coverage. File reading never supplies execution authority, rebinds the original plan or claims live preflight success; output failure preserves actual external state and leaves project bytes untouched. Native Restore effects now reject a changed current parent identity before mode changes and again before publication, unlink, rename or rmdir. Byte-equivalent inventories and retained file inodes do not authorize detached directory handles; this is a bounded native-race regression, not a sandbox claim. The renderer-free internal Restore invocation adapter now binds explicit argv and structured parameters to the existing native file and execution APIs. Public CLI registration, self-description, trusted real host authority wiring and complete Work integration remain unimplemented and mandatory; tested synthetic authorization grants no product/user approval. Targeted native Restore durability coverage now includes the independently journal-bound terminal barrier, before/after syscall faults, renewed authorization, retained originals and compatible legacy completion. The complete I/O/crash matrix, public trusted CLI host wiring, Work parity and all previously open specialist/lifecycle gates remain mandatory and partial. The passive work-restore-binding-v1 execution codec now retains both complete native byte objects as mandatory input-manifest entries, keeps original authoring and source identity distinct from current authority, and validates durable immutable generations. External plan transport locations do not alter unit identity; saved arguments cannot be rewritten in a trusted successor. Public CLI and trusted host wiring, planning Work, complete native recovery matrix, result delivery and full Work parity remain open. The closed embedding Restore Work executor now uses the native Restore/Recovery engine under a retained Work mutex with fresh host authorization and explicit current takeover. A separately supplied original-actor precondition binds existing native requests without replacing their current recovery actor. Real process exits preserve external checkpoints and before images; full-target completion and partial rollback remain native decisions even without the external source. This path returns a native outcome and leaves Work execution/delivery unconfirmed, with no public command or completed Work claim. A separate embedding owner-recovery adapter now preserves immutable, size/hash-bound original and replacement owner bytes and checkpoint binding, atomically exchanges only a natively proven dead local owner, and finishes an exactly matching interrupted transition with fresh consent. Actual Work writes and unresolved outer owner recovery are separate diagnostics from project Restore mutations. Native child-process exits test the handoff boundaries. Public command integration, complete progress/delivery and the full combined recovery matrix remain open; this is not Work completion or a release proof. A native progress adapter now confirms only the successful Restore execution unit and retains the original plan, actor, request, selection and complete native completion. Existing confirmed Work progress adds a native-completion precondition and cannot authorize a second publication. Real subprocess exits exercise combined Work and project recovery boundaries. Result delivery, completed Work, public CLI/structured integration, status/cancel/export parity and the remaining combined matrix stay open; no full-suite or release success is asserted. The internal native Restore Work coordinator now completes both declared units and durable finalization, retains original native findings and output variants, and replays terminal results from validated Work bytes without new project action. Genuine crashes retain the actual generation, fresh outer consent and unfinished native authorization gates. Public CLI/structured integration, planning-mode Work, status/cancel/export parity and remaining full Restore acceptance remain open; no release or full-suite success is asserted.
